content:
As consumers snapped up deals during Amazon's Prime Day, many discovered a rather interesting feature on the online shopping platform.

On Monday, Threads user Megan Montgomery posted a screenshot of the "About You" section of her Amazon account, writing: "I accidentally discovered a bunch of assumptions Amazon made about me based on my spending record, and I'm truly speechless."

Most of the list consists of innocuous statements, such as "owns a Kindle Paperwhite," "shops in the women's department," and "hosts themed parties." However, Montgomery circled one absolutely hilarious assertion: "has a flat butt."

Amazon users can easily find their personal customer profiles. Simply hover your cursor over your name on the homepage, select "Your Shopping preferences," then click "About You." You can also hover over your name, click "Account," and then go to "About You."

According to the company's corporate news site, this "About You" section was launched in May of this year. It uses AI to infer your personal details and preferences through information "including your conversations with Alexa for Shopping, product reviews you've written, your shopping history, items you've saved to Lists, and your search history."

After Montgomery's post went viral, others began posting screenshots of their own pages—some eerily accurate, some hilariously random, and some downright rude.

Although it doesn't seem you can completely disable this feature, customers can manually update their own pages (no doubt, over the past few days, people have already used this to add to the hilarious screenshot collection). Still, nothing is as funny as the random details generated by Amazon's AI tool.
